items.title: Here's what happened in crypto today
items.summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout
items.summary: China's five-year digital development plan calls for wider blockchain use in trade and manufacturing alongside stronger technical standards.

items.title: New York AG seeks $1.37B from NovaTech founders over Ponzi scheme
items.summary: The request follows an August 2025 default judgment, with the AG also announcing nearly $6 million in settlements with four promoters.

items.title: Bitcoin consolidates after 3% loss as AI fears stoke fresh stock-market weakness
items.summary: Bitcoin price volatility cooled as stock markets battled another day of resurgent AI fears during Friday's Asia trading session.

items.title: Was crypto self-custody ever designed for beginners?
items.summary: Recent hardware wallet security incidents have renewed debate over whether self-custody is suitable for beginners, as multisig and seedless designs carry their own risks.

items.title: Cysic dangles a 10% bounty, hacker pours loot into Tornado Cash
items.summary: The attacker moved $744,000 in ETH and BNB to Tornado Cash after exploiting Cysic's bridge to mint 10 million tokens on BNB Smart Chain.

items.title: Morning Minute: a16z Drops 'Crypto' From Its Fund
items.summary: The name change is symbolic of the fund's future investing focus, though the firm will continue investing in crypto.

items.title: Interpol Recovers $105M in African Cybercrime Sweep That Shut Illegal Crypto Mines
items.summary: Operation Serengeti III led to 1,462 arrests across 21 countries, while Angolan police seized more than 2,000 crypto mining devices.

items.title: Ethereum Delays Glamsterdam Testnet Fork Over Gas Security Flaws
items.summary: The Hoodi testnet fork is off after ChainSecurity found gas changes that could let contracts lock in failures, citing 13 real-world cases.

items.title: Heatbit's $899 Water Heater Element Mines Bitcoin While It Heats Your Tank
items.summary: The Bitwater element swaps a tank's resistance wire for 20 mining chips, and Heatbit says it uses the same electricity to heat the water.

items.title: Bitcoin in 'Wait and See Mode' And That Might Be a Good Thing
items.summary: BTC consolidates as traders await clearer signals from ETFs and macro.

items.title: a16z Drops Crypto From Its Name, Widens Bets to AI and Frontier Tech
items.summary: Andreessen Horowitz is renaming its crypto fund a16z Frontier and widening its scope to AI, autonomous machines and biology, saying the line between crypto and everyday tech has blurred.

items.title: Phantom rolls out Kalshi prediction markets to US users, says it's 'confident and comfortable' amid state lawsuits
items.summary: Phantom users will fund trades with CASH stablecoins, with market restrictions applied in Michigan, Nevada and Washington.

items.title: South Korea to amend forex law to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments: report
items.summary: South Korea is currently developing the Digital Asset Basic Act, which seeks to establish a comprehensive framework for crypto.

items.title: HSBC rolls out its first HKD stablecoin RedCoin to retail users
items.summary: PayMe users will be able to activate a stablecoin wallet in-app in the coming days for peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant payments.

items.title: Chainlink partners with LG CNS to drive Korean won stablecoin expansion
items.summary: LG CNS is set to integrate Chainlink's cross-chain, data, and orchestration infrastructure into its digital asset platform.

items.title: Grayscale expands in-kind subscriptions for crypto funds
items.summary: Grayscale expands in-kind subscriptions to 10 crypto funds, letting eligible investors swap tokens for shares without selling for cash.

items.title: Anza's Alpenglow goes live on Solana, cutting finality to 150 milliseconds
items.summary: Solana activated Alpenglow, replacing TowerBFT and cutting transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to about 150 milliseconds.

items.title: Coinbase Ireland's cash safeguards fell e5 million short before 2024 fix
items.summary: The regulator found no evidence of actual consumer harm, while an accepted €3.25 million penalty still needs High Court confirmation.

items.summary: Polling firm Wedgewood admitted on Oct. 20 that it fabricated most of its election surveys, and VoteHub, one of the aggregators that carried its results, is also the data source for recurring Kalshi contracts. items.title: Ethereum's long-awaited Glamsterdam upgrade hits another roadblock as 13 security risks emerge
items.summary: Ethereum developers have postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on a major test network after identifying potential security risks affecting existing smart contracts.

items.title: Robinhood generates $51 million in blockchain fees while Ethereum settlement costs total just $69000
items.summary: Bitwise's Q3 estimates put most fees with the operator before business expenses, while ARB and ETH offer different economic exposures.

items.title: A Midnight privacy-vault demo needs outside signers to release Ethereum tokens
items.summary: SIG's Ethereum example burns a shielded claim before payout, while restoring it after failure requires an attested outcome.

items.title: Bank of Korea Wants Stablecoins Written Into Forex Law as Crypto Bill and Tax Fight Come to a Head
items.summary: The Bank of Korea told lawmakers it will draft a forex law amendment this year to regulate stablecoins as a means of payment, a plan that points to tighter cross-border controls rather than legal-tender status.

items.title: Stand With Crypto Director: The Crypto Vote Will Decide the Midterms | Mason Lynaugh
items.summary: Ahead of midterms, Stand With Crypto's Mason Lynaugh breaks down a 3.1M-advocate push, explaining why crypto swing voters will forge the most pro-BTC Congress.

items.title: Parker Lewis: Bitcoin Will Settle 100% of Global Payments
items.summary: Parker Lewis argues Bitcoin will settle all global payments as $107T in debt strains the credit system, driving merchants toward zero-fee adoption.

items.title: Block Releases THE Bitcoin National Ad Campaign
items.summary: Block launches 'Bitcoin Does' to onboard millions. Head of Bitcoin Marketing Maria Pesce explains how the campaign focuses on real-world utility over tech.

items.title: Bloomberg's Mike McGlone: AI Risk Could Force Bitcoin Drawdown to $10,000

items.title: HSBC rolls out its first stablecoin to over 3 million everyday app users
items.summary: HSBC and Standard Chartered-led Anchorpoint received Hong Kong's first stablecoin issuer licenses in April. Anchorpoint began rolling out HKDAP in August.

items.title: Sweden's central bank revives e-krona debate as stablecoins and digital euro loom
items.summary: The Riksbank sees an e-krona as critical to securing national payments and monetary control.

items.title: Senate's top Democratic investigator looking into Tether payments to Bo Hines' firm
items.summary: Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat on the investigations subcommittee, added a probe of the ex-White House crypto adviser to his list of crypto interests.
